objective: Audit recent activation history and frontier decisions to determine whether explicit highest-value focused-task selection produces better information flow.
bottleneck: Prior activations had durable conclusions but task choice was opportunistic from a queue.
question: Does the current focused-task selector improve learning efficiency relative to the repository's prior opportunistic task choice?
action: Inspected the controller selector implementation (.github/scripts/campaign_controller.py task_rank/candidate_tasks_for_role), reconstructed its ranking over the live durable queue for both roles, and compared that ranking against the queue's stored order and against the historical activation record in state/LEARNING_STATE.md and state/activation_status.json.
verified: controller.task_rank is an ordinal tuple ordering (information gain, downstream leverage, falsification power, verifiability, then effort, complexity, execution risk, then task_id); candidate_tasks_for_role sorts OPEN tasks for the role by that key - read at .github/scripts/campaign_controller.py:198-225
reconstructed LEARNING_PROCESS ranking with P-001 OPEN = ['P-001','P-002','P-004','P-003','P-006','P-005'] (executed the controller's own task_rank over state/campaign/task_queue.json)
the selected task P-001 is the top-ranked candidate under both the selector and the stored queue order, so the selector did not alter which LEARNING_PROCESS task was chosen this activation

the only LP deviation from queue order is P-003/P-004, and their rank tuples differ solely in fields that are tied except the final task_id tiebreak ((0,0,1,0,1,1,0,'P-004') vs (0,0,1,0,1,0,0,'P-003') -> P-004 sorts first on complexity), so that deviation is an arbitrary lexicographic tiebreak, not a substantive priority difference

state/LEARNING_STATE.md records the frontier-first strategy delta as RETAIN (verified) across activations 37263008074, 37304873966, 37314710995, 37318950814, 37361000967, 37394344201, 37414038601 - each a distinct frontier cell closed with a decisive, independently verified verdict and no equivalent re-tests

state/campaign/global_agent_counter.json shows exactly one campaign (this run 43181285853, global slots 1-10, next=11), so the controller ordinal-rank selector has no prior completed campaign and no post-selection outcome evidence exists anywhere in durable state
state/campaign/runs/43181285853/campaign_status.json completed_agents=[] and the run agents directory contains only agent_01 contract/before/log artifacts - no agent 02-10 records exist yet
unverified: No post-selection outcome evidence exists for the controller ordinal-rank selector: agents 02-10 have not run, so any claim that the selector improves learning efficiency relative to prior opportunistic choice is UNVERIFIED

The repository's prior activations (the LEARNING_STATE demonstrations) predate the controller selector (first campaign is this run), so they evidence the frontier-first delta, not the ordinal-rank selector, and cannot be used as a selector A/B comparison

The only substantive selector effect observed - ranking HIGHER_ORDER task R-003 (unresolved volatility-gate mechanism) above R-005 (refinement of the already-admitted momentum effect) - is a design inspection consistent with the documented uncertainty-reduction principle, but it has not been executed and produced no outcome evidence
git command inspection was denied at this layer (project bash deny rule), so commit-level provenance of when campaign_controller.py's selector was introduced was not independently checked
observed_effect: The selector is behaviourally a no-op on the current LEARNING_PROCESS queue modulo an arbitrary task_id tiebreak (P-001 chosen either way; P-003/P-004 swap only on tied benefit fields). It reorders HIGHER_ORDER candidates substantively (R-003 above R-005). No campaign outcome data exists to show that either reordering improved information flow, so no selector advantage is demonstrated.
uncertainty_targeted: Whether the controller's ordinal-rank focused-task selector improves learning efficiency relative to the repository's prior opportunistic queue choice.
uncertainty_reduced: Partial: the mechanism is now precisely characterized (a benefit-first ordinal sort whose only LEARNING_PROCESS deviation is a tiebreak, and whose only substantive deviation is an untested HIGHER_ORDER reordering); the effectiveness question remains open because no post-selection outcome exists. This narrows the remaining uncertainty to a single executable comparison (agents 02-10 outcomes vs the documented frontier-first baseline).
research_result: No research experiment was run; this is a process audit. Durable evidence shows the prior frontier-first process closed five frontier cells (reversal, CSRS, volatility targeting, momentum, cross-sectional momentum) and one breakout cell each exactly once with decisive independently-verified verdicts and no equivalent re-tests, so the learning process was already effective without the selector. The selector's incremental value over that baseline is not evidenced.
next: Re-run this selector-effectiveness question after campaign 43181285853 agents 02-10 produce durable outcome records, comparing information gained per activation under the selector against the documented frontier-first baseline.

candidate_tasks.primary_question: Do the completed agent records from campaign 43181285853 show higher information gained per activation under the ordinal-rank selector than the documented frontier-first baseline?
candidate_tasks.bottleneck: The controller selector's effectiveness is unmeasured because no post-selection outcome evidence exists yet.
candidate_tasks.objective: Once agents 02-10 finish, compare per-activation information-gain classifications (falsified / strengthened / repaired / new evidence / no gain) under the selector against the prior frontier-first activation record.
candidate_tasks.scope: Durable agent records and LEARNING_STATE only; no new experiments, no controller changes.
candidate_tasks.out_of_scope: Do not modify controller architecture, add a reward score, or rerun historical experiments.
candidate_tasks.deliverable: A bounded RETAIN/REJECT/UNVERIFIED judgment on selector effectiveness with per-activation evidence.
candidate_tasks.success_criterion: A clear classification of selector effectiveness or an explicit statement that the campaign evidence remains insufficient.
candidate_tasks.stop_condition: Stop when the campaign records are sufficient to classify selector effectiveness or clearly insufficient.
candidate_tasks.verification_requirement: Controller-side validation plus independent inspection of cited agent records.
candidate_tasks.evidence_basis: This activation (P-001) established that no post-selection outcome evidence exists yet.
